ko.title: 선거 당일에 개표가 거의 끝나지 않는 이유: 표는 어떻게 집계되며 결과는 언제 예상할 수 있는가

segments.src: For many Americans, election night means staying up late, watching a map fill in with color and waiting for a winner to be named.
segments.tr: 많은 미국인들에게 선거 당일 밤은 늦게까지 깨어 지도를 색으로 채워 나가는 모습을 지켜보며 승자가 발표되기를 기다리는 것을 의미합니다.

segments.src: In practice, the picture on election night is often incomplete.
segments.tr: 실제로는 선거 당일 밤의 개표 상황이 불완전한 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: Counting continues for days in some places, and that is usually a sign the system is working as designed, not a sign that something has gone wrong.
segments.tr: 일부 지역에서는 며칠 동안 개표가 계속되기도 하는데, 이는 무언가 잘못되었다는 신호가 아니라 보통 시스템이 설계된 대로 작동하고 있다는 신호입니다.

segments.src: This guide explains why results take time, how counting differs from state to state, and what to look for before treating any early tally as final.
segments.tr: 이 가이드는 결과가 나오기까지 시간이 걸리는 이유, 주마다 개표 방식이 어떻게 다른지, 그리고 초기 집계를 최종 결과로 간주하기 전에 무엇을 살펴봐야 하는지 설명합니다.

segments.src: ## Unofficial results come first, official results come later
segments.tr: ## 비공식 결과가 먼저 나오고, 공식 결과는 나중에 나옵니다

segments.src: The numbers you see on election night are **unofficial**.
segments.tr: 선거 당일 밤에 보는 숫자는 **비공식** 숫자입니다.

segments.src: News organizations and election offices report running totals as counties finish processing ballots.
segments.tr: 언론사와 선거 관리 사무소는 각 카운티가 투표지 처리를 완료함에 따라 누적 집계치를 발표합니다.

segments.src: Official results come only after a process called **canvassing**, in which local and state officials check the totals, reconcile them against records of voters and ballots, and certify the outcome.
segments.tr: 공식 결과는 지방 및 주 당국자가 집계 수치를 확인하고, 이를 유권자 및 투표지 기록과 대조하여 결과를 인증하는 **검표(canvassing)** 절차를 거친 후에야 나옵니다.

segments.src: Canvassing and certification can take from several days to several weeks, depending on the state.
segments.tr: 검표 및 인증 과정은 주에 따라 며칠에서 몇 주까지 걸릴 수 있습니다.

segments.src: During that period, officials add late-arriving ballots, resolve problems with incomplete ballots, and correct clerical errors.
segments.tr: 이 기간 동안 당국자들은 늦게 도착한 투표지를 추가하고, 불완전한 투표지의 문제를 해결하며, 기밀상의 단순 오기를 수정합니다.

segments.src: Small changes in totals during this stage are normal.
segments.tr: 이 단계에서 총 집계 수치에 약간의 변화가 일어나는 것은 정상입니다.

segments.src: ## Why counting takes time
segments.tr: ## 개표에 시간이 걸리는 이유

segments.src: Several things make a fast count hard.
segments.tr: 빠른 개표를 어렵게 만드는 몇 가지 요인이 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Mail ballots take more steps to process.** A ballot returned by mail usually needs its envelope opened, its signature or identifying information checked, the ballot removed, flattened and scanned, and the voter's record updated. An in-person ballot cast on a machine skips most of these steps.
segments.tr: - **우편 투표는 처리 단계가 더 많습니다.** 우편으로 반송된 투표지는 보통 봉투를 열고, 서명이나 신원 확인 정보를 검증하며, 투표지를 꺼내 펴서 스캔하고, 유권자 기록을 업데이트해야 합니다. 기계로 행사하는 현장 투표는 이러한 단계 대부분을 건너뜁니다.

segments.src: - **Rules about when processing can begin differ.** In some states, election workers may start preparing mail ballots weeks before Election Day. In others, they may not begin until Election Day itself, which pushes the work back.
segments.tr: - **처리 시작 시점에 관한 규정이 다릅니다.** 일부 주에서는 선거 사무원들이 Election Day 몇 주 전부터 우편 투표지 준비를 시작할 수 있습니다. 다른 주에서는 Election Day 당일이 되어야 시작할 수 있어 작업이 뒤로 밀리게 됩니다.

segments.src: - **Deadlines for late-arriving ballots differ.** Some states accept mail ballots that arrive after Election Day as long as they were postmarked on time. Others require ballots to arrive by the close of polls. Where a grace period exists, the final count cannot be known until it ends.
segments.tr: - **늦게 도착하는 우편 투표지의 마감 시한이 다릅니다.** 일부 주에서는 제시간에 소인이 찍혔다면 Election Day 이후에 도착한 우편 투표지도 인정합니다. 다른 주에서는 투표 종료 시점까지 투표지가 도착해야 합니다. 유예 기간이 존재하는 곳에서는 해당 기간이 끝날 때까지 최종 집계를 알 수 없습니다.

segments.src: - **Voters can fix some problems.** Many states let voters correct issues such as a missing signature through a process often called "curing." Provisional ballots, which are used when a voter's eligibility needs to be confirmed, are also reviewed after Election Day.
segments.tr: - **유권자가 일부 문제를 보완할 수 있습니다.** 많은 주에서 유권자가 누락된 서명과 같은 문제를 해결할 수 있도록 "치유(curing)"라고 불리는 절차를 제공합니다. 유권자 자격 확인이 필요한 경우 사용되는 임시 투표지(Provisional ballots) 역시 Election Day 이후에 검토됩니다.

segments.src: - **Counties report at different speeds.** A small county with few ballots may finish within hours. A large, populous county may take much longer. The order in which counties report can make a race appear to swing even though no individual vote has changed.
segments.tr: - **카운티마다 보고 속도가 다릅니다.** 투표지가 적은 작은 카운티는 몇 시간 만에 끝날 수 있습니다. 인구가 많은 대형 카운티는 훨씬 더 오래 걸릴 수 있습니다. 개별 표는 하나도 바뀌지 않았음에도 카운티들이 보고하는 순서에 따라 경선 양상이 역전되는 것처럼 보일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Why early tallies can shift
segments.tr: ## 초기 집계가 변동될 수 있는 이유

segments.src: Early totals can look lopsided for a simple reason: the votes counted first are not a random sample of all votes.
segments.tr: 초기 집계가 한쪽으로 쏠려 보일 수 있는 단순한 이유는 먼저 개표된 표가 전체 표의 무작위 표본이 아니기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Which ballots come in first depends on the state's rules and on how each county reports.
segments.tr: 어떤 투표지가 먼저 들어오는지는 주의 규정과 각 카운티의 보고 방식에 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: In one state, in-person votes may be tallied first, followed by mail ballots.
segments.tr: 어떤 주에서는 현장 투표가 먼저 집계되고 우편 투표가 그 뒤를 이을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: In another, early and mail votes may be released first, and Election Day votes later.
segments.tr: 다른 주에서는 조기 투표 및 우편 투표가 먼저 공개되고 Election Day 현장 투표가 나중에 공개될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Either way, the leader at 10 p.m.
segments.tr: 어느 쪽이든 오후 10시 시점의 선두가

segments.src: may not be the leader once everything is counted.
segments.tr: 모든 개표가 끝난 후에도 선두가 아닐 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Analysts sometimes call this a "red shift" or "blue shift," depending on which direction it runs, but the direction varies by state and by year.
segments.tr: 분석가들은 방향에 따라 이를 "레드 Shift" 또는 "블루 Shift"라고 부르기도 하지만, 그 방향은 주와 연도에 따라 다릅니다.

segments.src: The shift reflects the order of reporting, not irregularities.
segments.tr: 이러한 변동은 보고 순서를 반영하는 것일 뿐 부정행위를 의미하지 않습니다.

segments.src: ## How the order of counting varies by state
segments.tr: ## 주별로 개표 순서가 다른 방식

segments.src: States set their own election procedures, so there is no single national timeline.
segments.tr: 각 주가 자체 선거 절차를 설정하므로 단일한 전국 표준 일정은 없습니다.

segments.src: These are general patterns, and details change, so always check your own state's election office.
segments.tr: 다음은 일반적인 패턴이며 세부 사항은 변경될 수 있으므로 항상 해당 주의 선거 관리 사무소를 확인하세요.

segments.src: - **States that process mail ballots early** often report a large share of results quickly, because most ballots are ready to be tabulated when polls close.
segments.tr: - **우편 투표를 일찍 처리하는 주**는 투표소가 닫힐 때 대부분의 투표지가 즉시 집계될 준비가 되어 있어 빠르게 많은 비율의 결과를 보고하는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: - **States that restrict early processing** tend to report in stages, with a large batch of mail ballots appearing later in the night or in the following days.
segments.tr: - **사전 처리를 제한하는 주**는 단계를 나누어 보고하는 경향이 있어, 밤 늦게나 다음 날에 대규모 우편 투표지 묶음이 나타납니다.

segments.src: - **States with grace periods for mail ballots** may not be able to finalize results until the deadline for late-arriving ballots passes.
segments.tr: - **우편 투표 유예 기간이 있는 주**는 늦게 도착하는 투표지의 마감 시한이 지날 때까지 결과를 확정하지 못할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **States with high volumes of mail voting** may need extra days simply because of the number of envelopes to process.
segments.tr: - **우편 투표 비율이 높은 주**는 단순히 처리해야 할 봉투의 수 때문에 추가 며칠이 필요할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Rules change from one election cycle to the next, so last cycle's timeline is a useful guide but not a guarantee.
segments.tr: 규정은 선거 주기마다 변경되므로 지난 주기의 타임라인은 유용한 참고 자료일 뿐 보장되지는 않습니다.

segments.src: ## How news organizations decide a race is over
segments.tr: ## 언론사가 승패를 판정하는 방식

segments.src: When a news organization says a candidate has won, it is making a projection, not announcing a certified result.
segments.tr: 언론사가 특정 후보의 승리를 선언할 때, 이는 예측(projection)을 발표하는 것이지 인증된 결과를 발표하는 것이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Newsrooms and the Associated Press use vote counts, the number of ballots still outstanding, where those ballots are from, and historical voting patterns to judge whether a trailing candidate can still catch up.
segments.tr: 보도국과 AP 통신(Associated Press)은 득표수, 남아 있는 미개표 투표지 수, 해당 투표지의 출처 지역, 과거 투표 패턴 등을 종합하여 뒤처진 후보가 역전할 수 있는지 판단합니다.

segments.src: A race is typically called only when the remaining ballots cannot plausibly change the outcome.
segments.tr: 일반적으로 남은 투표지로 결과가 뒤바뀔 가능성이 없을 때만 승자 판정을 내립니다.

segments.src: Calls can differ by outlet.
segments.tr: 매체마다 승자 판정 시점이 다를 수 있습니다.

segments.src: A close race may stay uncalled for days, and that caution is deliberate.
segments.tr: 접전 지역은 며칠 동안 승자 미정 상태로 남아 있을 수 있으며, 이러한 신중함은 의도적인 것입니다.

segments.src: ## Close races, recounts and audits
segments.tr: ## 초박빙 경선, 재개표 및 감사

segments.src: When the margin is very narrow, a recount may happen automatically under state law or at the request of a candidate.
segments.tr: 표 차이가 매우 근소한 경우, 주 법에 따라 자동으로 또는 후보의 요청에 의해 재개표가 진행될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Many states also run post-election audits, which check a sample of ballots against the machine totals to confirm the equipment counted accurately.
segments.tr: 또한 많은 주에서 선거 후 감사를 실시하여 표본 투표지를 기계 집계치와 대조함으로써 장비가 정확하게 집계했는지 확인합니다.

segments.src: Recounts rarely change the result by more than a small number of votes, but they can add time before a race is settled.
segments.tr: 재개표로 결과가 크게 바뀌는 경우는 드물지만, 경선 확정까지 시간이 더 걸릴 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## What to watch before declaring any race over
segments.tr: ## 경선 종료를 선언하기 전에 확인해야 할 사항

segments.src: A few questions can help you read election night results sensibly:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 질문은 선거 당일 밤의 결과를 분별 있게 해석하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

segments.src: 1. **How much of the vote is in?** A percentage reporting figure helps, but it can mislead if the remaining ballots come from areas that lean differently.
segments.tr: 1. **전체 개표가 얼마나 진행되었는가?** 개표율 수치가 도움이 되지만, 남은 투표지가 성향이 다른 지역에서 나온 경우 오해를 불러일으킬 수 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. **Which ballots are outstanding?** Mail ballots, provisional ballots and ballots from large counties can all change a total.
segments.tr: 2. **어떤 투표지가 아직 남아 있는가?** 우편 투표, 임시 투표, 대형 카운티의 투표지 모두 총집계를 바꿀 수 있습니다.

segments.src: 3. **What are the state's deadlines?** Check whether late-arriving mail ballots will still be counted and when canvassing ends.
segments.tr: 3. **해당 주의 마감 시한은 언제인가?** 늦게 도착한 우편 투표지가 계속 집계되는지, 검표가 언제 끝나는지 확인하세요.

segments.src: 4. **What is the margin?** A large lead with few ballots left is very different from a narrow lead with many left.
segments.tr: 4. **격차는 얼마인가?** 표가 얼마 남지 않은 상태에서의 큰 리드는 표가 많이 남은 상태에서의 근소한 리드와 전혀 다릅니다.

segments.src: 5. **Who is reporting the result?** Rely on your state or county election office for official information, and on established news organizations for projections.
segments.tr: 5. **누가 결과를 발표하고 있는가?** 공식 정보는 해당 주 또는 카운티 선거 관리 사무소에 의존하고, 예측 결과는 공인된 언론사에 의존하세요.

segments.src: ## Practical tips for voters
segments.tr: ## 유권자를 위한 실용적인 조언

segments.src: - Expect that some races will not be called on election night, and treat that as normal.
segments.tr: - 일부 경선은 선거 당일 밤에 승자가 판정되지 않을 수 있음을 예상하고, 이를 정상적인 현상으로 받아들이세요.

segments.src: - Look up your state's election office website for its timeline for counting, curing and certification.
segments.tr: - 해당 주 선거 관리 사무소 웹사이트에서 개표, 치유(curing) 및 인증 관련 일정을 확인하세요.

segments.src: - Be cautious about screenshots and unverified claims on social media, especially in the hours when totals are changing fast.
segments.tr: - 특히 집계 수치가 빠르게 변하는 시간대에는 소셜 미디어의 스크린샷이나 검증되지 않은 주장에 주의하세요.

segments.src: - Remember that "not yet counted" is not the same as "missing" or "lost."
segments.tr: - "아직 개표되지 않음"이 "누락됨" 또는 "분실됨"과 같은 의미가 아님을 기억하세요.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 요약

segments.src: A slow count is not a failed count.
segments.tr: 느린 개표가 실패한 개표는 아닙니다.

segments.src: Accuracy takes time, and the steps that take the longest, such as verifying mail ballots, curing errors and canvassing, are the same steps that protect the integrity of the result.
segments.tr: 정확성에는 시간이 걸리며, 우편 투표 검증, 오류 치유, 검표와 같이 가장 오래 걸리는 단계들이 바로 결과의 무결성을 보호하는 단계입니다.

segments.src: When you follow election night coverage, treat early totals as a snapshot, pay attention to what is still outstanding, and wait for officials to certify the final numbers.
segments.tr: 선거 당일 밤 보도를 지켜볼 때 초기 집계는 단지 일시적인 스냅샷으로 받아들이고, 아직 남아 있는 개표에 주목하며, 당국이 최종 수치를 인증할 때까지 기다리세요.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only and does not describe the rules of any specific jurisdiction.
segments.tr: *본 기사는 일반적인 정보 제공만을 목적으로 하며 특정 관할 구역의 규정을 설명하지 않습니다.

segments.src: Check your local election office for current procedures and deadlines.*
segments.tr: 최신 절차 및 마감 시한은 해당 지역 선거 관리 사무소에서 확인하세요.*

zh.title: 为什么选举之夜很少在选举之夜结束：选票如何统计以及何时公布结果

segments.src: For many Americans, election night means staying up late, watching a map fill in with color and waiting for a winner to be named.
segments.tr: 对于许多美国人来说，选举之夜意味着熬夜，看着地图被颜色填满，等待获胜者宣布。

segments.src: In practice, the picture on election night is often incomplete.
segments.tr: 实际上，选举之夜的情况往往是不完整的。

segments.src: Counting continues for days in some places, and that is usually a sign the system is working as designed, not a sign that something has gone wrong.
segments.tr: 在某些地方，计票工作会持续数天，这通常是系统按设计运行的标志，而不是出现问题的迹象。

segments.src: This guide explains why results take time, how counting differs from state to state, and what to look for before treating any early tally as final.
segments.tr: 本指南解释了为什么结果需要时间、各州的计票方式有何不同，以及在将任何早期统计结果视为最终结果之前需要注意什么。

segments.src: ## Unofficial results come first, official results come later
segments.tr: ## 非官方结果先行，官方结果随后

segments.src: The numbers you see on election night are **unofficial**.
segments.tr: 您在选举之夜看到的数字是**非官方的**。

segments.src: News organizations and election offices report running totals as counties finish processing ballots.
segments.tr: 随着各县完成选票处理，新闻机构和选举办公室会报告当前的统计总数。

segments.src: Official results come only after a process called **canvassing**, in which local and state officials check the totals, reconcile them against records of voters and ballots, and certify the outcome.
segments.tr: 官方结果只有在经过称为**计票核实（canvassing）**的过程后才会产生，在此过程中，地方和州官员会核对总数，将其与选民和选票记录进行核对，并认证结果。

segments.src: Canvassing and certification can take from several days to several weeks, depending on the state.
segments.tr: 根据各州的不同，计票核实和认证可能需要几天到几周的时间。

segments.src: During that period, officials add late-arriving ballots, resolve problems with incomplete ballots, and correct clerical errors.
segments.tr: 在此期间，官员会添加迟到的选票，解决不完整选票的问题，并纠正文书错误。

segments.src: Small changes in totals during this stage are normal.
segments.tr: 在此阶段总数发生微小变化是正常的。

segments.src: ## Why counting takes time
segments.tr: ## 为什么计票需要时间

segments.src: Several things make a fast count hard.
segments.tr: 有几件事使得快速计票变得困难。

segments.src: - **Mail ballots take more steps to process.** A ballot returned by mail usually needs its envelope opened, its signature or identifying information checked, the ballot removed, flattened and scanned, and the voter's record updated. An in-person ballot cast on a machine skips most of these steps.
segments.tr: - **邮寄选票的处理步骤更多。** 邮寄回来的选票通常需要拆开信封、检查签名或身份信息、取出选票、展平并扫描，然后更新选民记录。而在机器上投下的现场选票则跳过了大部分这些步骤。

segments.src: - **Rules about when processing can begin differ.** In some states, election workers may start preparing mail ballots weeks before Election Day. In others, they may not begin until Election Day itself, which pushes the work back.
segments.tr: - **关于何时开始处理的规定各不相同。** 在一些州，选举工作人员可以在选举日之前几周开始准备邮寄选票。而在另一些州，他们可能要到选举日当天才能开始，这推迟了工作进度。

segments.src: - **Deadlines for late-arriving ballots differ.** Some states accept mail ballots that arrive after Election Day as long as they were postmarked on time. Others require ballots to arrive by the close of polls. Where a grace period exists, the final count cannot be known until it ends.
segments.tr: - **迟到选票的截止日期各不相同。** 一些州接受在选举日之后到达的邮寄选票，只要它们在截止日期前盖有邮戳即可。另一些州则要求选票必须在投票结束前送达。如果存在宽限期，那么在宽限期结束之前，最终计票结果是无法得知的。

segments.src: - **Voters can fix some problems.** Many states let voters correct issues such as a missing signature through a process often called "curing." Provisional ballots, which are used when a voter's eligibility needs to be confirmed, are also reviewed after Election Day.
segments.tr: - **选民可以解决一些问题。** 许多州允许选民通过通常称为“补救（curing）”的过程来纠正诸如缺少签名之类的问题。在需要确认选民资格时使用的临时选票，也会在选举日之后进行审查。

segments.src: - **Counties report at different speeds.** A small county with few ballots may finish within hours. A large, populous county may take much longer. The order in which counties report can make a race appear to swing even though no individual vote has changed.
segments.tr: - **各县报告的速度不同。** 选票较少的小县可能在几小时内完成。人口众多的大县可能需要更长时间。各县报告的顺序可能会使竞选看起来发生了摇摆，即使没有任何个人选票发生变化。

segments.src: ## Why early tallies can shift
segments.tr: ## 为什么早期统计结果会发生变化

segments.src: Early totals can look lopsided for a simple reason: the votes counted first are not a random sample of all votes.
segments.tr: 早期统计结果看起来不平衡的原因很简单：首先统计的选票并不是所有选票的随机样本。

segments.src: Which ballots come in first depends on the state's rules and on how each county reports.
segments.tr: 哪些选票先被统计取决于各州的规定以及每个县的报告方式。

segments.src: In one state, in-person votes may be tallied first, followed by mail ballots.
segments.tr: 在一个州，现场投票可能会先被统计，随后是邮寄选票。

segments.src: In another, early and mail votes may be released first, and Election Day votes later.
segments.tr: 在另一个州，提前投票和邮寄选票可能会先公布，选举日的投票则稍后公布。

segments.src: Either way, the leader at 10 p.m.
segments.tr: 无论哪种方式，晚上10点的领先者

segments.src: may not be the leader once everything is counted.
segments.tr: 在所有选票统计完毕后可能不再是领先者。

segments.src: Analysts sometimes call this a "red shift" or "blue shift," depending on which direction it runs, but the direction varies by state and by year.
segments.tr: 分析人士有时称之为“红色转移”或“蓝色转移”，具体取决于它运行的方向，但方向因州和年份而异。

segments.src: The shift reflects the order of reporting, not irregularities.
segments.tr: 这种转移反映的是报告的顺序，而不是违规行为。

segments.src: ## How the order of counting varies by state
segments.tr: ## 各州计票顺序的差异

segments.src: States set their own election procedures, so there is no single national timeline.
segments.tr: 各州制定自己的选举程序，因此没有统一的全国时间表。

segments.src: These are general patterns, and details change, so always check your own state's election office.
segments.tr: 这些是一般模式，细节会发生变化，因此请务必查看您所在州的选举办公室。

segments.src: - **States that process mail ballots early** often report a large share of results quickly, because most ballots are ready to be tabulated when polls close.
segments.tr: - **提前处理邮寄选票的州**通常会很快报告很大一部分结果，因为大多数选票在投票结束时已准备好进行制表。

segments.src: - **States that restrict early processing** tend to report in stages, with a large batch of mail ballots appearing later in the night or in the following days.
segments.tr: - **限制提前处理的州**往往分阶段报告，大量邮寄选票会在当晚晚些时候或随后的几天出现。

segments.src: - **States with grace periods for mail ballots** may not be able to finalize results until the deadline for late-arriving ballots passes.
segments.tr: - **对邮寄选票设有宽限期的州**可能要等到迟到选票的截止日期过后才能确定最终结果。

segments.src: - **States with high volumes of mail voting** may need extra days simply because of the number of envelopes to process.
segments.tr: - **邮寄投票量大的州**可能仅仅因为需要处理的信封数量多而需要额外的时间。

segments.src: Rules change from one election cycle to the next, so last cycle's timeline is a useful guide but not a guarantee.
segments.tr: 规则在不同的选举周期之间会发生变化，因此上一个周期的时间表是一个有用的指南，但不能作为保证。

segments.src: ## How news organizations decide a race is over
segments.tr: ## 新闻机构如何判定竞选结束

segments.src: When a news organization says a candidate has won, it is making a projection, not announcing a certified result.
segments.tr: 当新闻机构宣布某位候选人获胜时，它是在进行预测，而不是宣布认证结果。

segments.src: Newsrooms and the Associated Press use vote counts, the number of ballots still outstanding, where those ballots are from, and historical voting patterns to judge whether a trailing candidate can still catch up.
segments.tr: 新闻编辑室和美联社（Associated Press）使用投票统计数据、尚未统计的选票数量、这些选票的来源以及历史投票模式来判断落后的候选人是否仍能追赶上来。

segments.src: A race is typically called only when the remaining ballots cannot plausibly change the outcome.
segments.tr: 竞选通常只有在剩余选票无法合理改变结果时才会被宣布结束。

segments.src: Calls can differ by outlet.
segments.tr: 不同媒体的宣布结果可能有所不同。

segments.src: A close race may stay uncalled for days, and that caution is deliberate.
segments.tr: 势均力敌的竞选可能会持续数天没有结果，这种谨慎是有意为之的。

segments.src: ## Close races, recounts and audits
segments.tr: ## 势均力敌的竞选、重新计票和审计

segments.src: When the margin is very narrow, a recount may happen automatically under state law or at the request of a candidate.
segments.tr: 当差距非常小时，根据州法律或应候选人要求，可能会自动进行重新计票。

segments.src: Many states also run post-election audits, which check a sample of ballots against the machine totals to confirm the equipment counted accurately.
segments.tr: 许多州还会进行选举后审计，将抽样的选票与机器统计的总数进行核对，以确认设备统计准确。

segments.src: Recounts rarely change the result by more than a small number of votes, but they can add time before a race is settled.
segments.tr: 重新计票很少会改变超过少量选票的结果，但它们可能会增加竞选结果确定前的时间。

segments.src: ## What to watch before declaring any race over
segments.tr: ## 在宣布任何竞选结束前需要观察什么

segments.src: A few questions can help you read election night results sensibly:
segments.tr: 几个问题可以帮助您理智地解读选举之夜的结果：

segments.src: 1. **How much of the vote is in?** A percentage reporting figure helps, but it can mislead if the remaining ballots come from areas that lean differently.
segments.tr: 1. **已统计了多少选票？** 报告百分比数字有帮助，但如果剩余选票来自倾向不同的地区，它可能会产生误导。

segments.src: 2. **Which ballots are outstanding?** Mail ballots, provisional ballots and ballots from large counties can all change a total.
segments.tr: 2. **哪些选票尚未统计？** 邮寄选票、临时选票和大县的选票都可能改变总数。

segments.src: 3. **What are the state's deadlines?** Check whether late-arriving mail ballots will still be counted and when canvassing ends.
segments.tr: 3. **各州的截止日期是什么？** 查看迟到的邮寄选票是否仍会被统计，以及计票核实何时结束。

segments.src: 4. **What is the margin?** A large lead with few ballots left is very different from a narrow lead with many left.
segments.tr: 4. **差距是多少？** 剩余选票很少时的大幅领先与剩余选票很多时的小幅领先是非常不同的。

segments.src: 5. **Who is reporting the result?** Rely on your state or county election office for official information, and on established news organizations for projections.
segments.tr: 5. **谁在报告结果？** 依靠您所在州或县的选举办公室获取官方信息，依靠成熟的新闻机构获取预测。

segments.src: ## Practical tips for voters
segments.tr: ## 给选民的实用建议

segments.src: - Expect that some races will not be called on election night, and treat that as normal.
segments.tr: - 预计有些竞选不会在选举之夜宣布结果，并将此视为正常现象。

segments.src: - Look up your state's election office website for its timeline for counting, curing and certification.
segments.tr: - 在您所在州的选举办公室网站上查找其计票、补救和认证的时间表。

segments.src: - Be cautious about screenshots and unverified claims on social media, especially in the hours when totals are changing fast.
segments.tr: - 对社交媒体上的截图和未经证实的说法要保持谨慎，尤其是在总数快速变化的几个小时内。

segments.src: - Remember that "not yet counted" is not the same as "missing" or "lost."
segments.tr: - 请记住，“尚未统计”并不等同于“丢失”或“遗失”。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: A slow count is not a failed count.
segments.tr: 缓慢的计票并不是失败的计票。

segments.src: Accuracy takes time, and the steps that take the longest, such as verifying mail ballots, curing errors and canvassing, are the same steps that protect the integrity of the result.
segments.tr: 准确性需要时间，而耗时最长的步骤，例如验证邮寄选票、纠正错误和计票核实，正是保护结果完整性的步骤。

segments.src: When you follow election night coverage, treat early totals as a snapshot, pay attention to what is still outstanding, and wait for officials to certify the final numbers.
segments.tr: 当您关注选举之夜的报道时，请将早期统计结果视为快照，注意还有什么尚未统计，并等待官员认证最终数字。

segments.src: *This article is for general information only and does not describe the rules of any specific jurisdiction.
segments.tr: *本文仅供一般参考，并未描述任何特定司法管辖区的规则。

segments.src: Check your local election office for current procedures and deadlines.*
segments.tr: 请查看您当地的选举办公室以了解当前的程序和截止日期。*

hi.title: चुनाव की रात ही परिणाम पर समाप्त क्यों नहीं होती: वोटों की गिनती कैसे होती है और नतीजों की उम्मीद कब करें

segments.src: For many Americans, election night means staying up late, watching a map fill in with color and waiting for a winner to be named.

segments.src: In practice, the picture on election night is often incomplete.

segments.src: Counting continues for days in some places, and that is usually a sign the system is working as designed, not a sign that something has gone wrong.
segments.tr: कुछ स्थानों पर गिनती कई दिनों तक चलती है, और यह आमतौर पर इस बात का संकेत है कि प्रणाली योजना के अनुसार काम कर रही है, न कि यह कि कुछ गलत हुआ है।

segments.tr: यह मार्गदर्शिका बताती है कि परिणामों में समय क्यों लगता है, राज्यों में गिनती के नियम कैसे भिन्न होते हैं, और किसी भी शुरुआती आंकड़े को अंतिम मानने से पहले क्या ध्यान रखना चाहिए।

segments.src: ## Unofficial results come first, official results come later
segments.tr: ## अनौपचारिक परिणाम पहले आते हैं, आधिकारिक परिणाम बाद में

segments.src: The numbers you see on election night are **unofficial**.
segments.tr: चुनाव की रात आप जो आंकड़े देखते हैं वे **अनौपचारिक** होते हैं।

segments.src: News organizations and election offices report running totals as counties finish processing ballots.
segments.tr: समाचार संगठन और चुनाव कार्यालय चालू आंकड़ों की रिपोर्ट करते हैं जैसे-जैसे काउंटी मतपत्रों को संसाधित करना पूरा करती हैं।

segments.src: Official results come only after a process called **canvassing**, in which local and state officials check the totals, reconcile them against records of voters and ballots, and certify the outcome.
segments.tr: आधिकारिक परिणाम केवल **कैनवासिंग (जांच)** नामक प्रक्रिया के बाद आते हैं, जिसमें स्थानीय और राज्य अधिकारी कुल योगों की जांच करते हैं, मतदाताओं और मतपत्रों के रिकॉर्ड के साथ उनका मिलान करते हैं, और परिणाम को प्रमाणित करते हैं।

segments.src: Canvassing and certification can take from several days to several weeks, depending on the state.
segments.tr: राज्य के आधार पर कैनवासिंग और प्रमाणीकरण में कई दिनों से लेकर कई सप्ताह तक का समय लग सकता है।

segments.src: During that period, officials add late-arriving ballots, resolve problems with incomplete ballots, and correct clerical errors.
segments.tr: उस अवधि के दौरान, अधिकारी देर से आने वाले मतपत्रों को जोड़ते हैं, अधूरे मतपत्रों की समस्याओं का समाधान करते हैं, और लिपिकीय त्रुटियों को सुधारते हैं।

segments.src: Small changes in totals during this stage are normal.
segments.tr: इस चरण के दौरान कुल आंकड़ों में छोटे बदलाव होना सामान्य है।

segments.src: ## Why counting takes time
segments.tr: ## गिनती में समय क्यों लगता है

segments.src: Several things make a fast count hard.
segments.tr: कई चीजें तेज़ी से गिनती करना मुश्किल बनाती हैं।

segments.src: - **Mail ballots take more steps to process.** A ballot returned by mail usually needs its envelope opened, its signature or identifying information checked, the ballot removed, flattened and scanned, and the voter's record updated. An in-person ballot cast on a machine skips most of these steps.
segments.tr: - **डाक मतपत्रों को संसाधित करने में अधिक चरण लगते हैं।** डाक द्वारा लौटाए गए मतपत्र के लिफाफे को खोलने, उसके हस्ताक्षर या पहचान की जानकारी की जांच करने, मतपत्र को निकालने, सीधा करने और स्कैन करने, और मतदाता के रिकॉर्ड को अपडेट करने की आवश्यकता होती है। मशीन पर व्यक्तिगत रूप से डाला गया मतपत्र इनमें से अधिकांश चरणों को छोड़ देता है।

segments.src: - **Rules about when processing can begin differ.** In some states, election workers may start preparing mail ballots weeks before Election Day. In others, they may not begin until Election Day itself, which pushes the work back.
segments.tr: - **प्रसंस्करण कब शुरू हो सकता है, इसके नियम अलग-अलग हैं।** कुछ राज्यों में, चुनाव कार्यकर्ता चुनाव के दिन से कई हफ्ते पहले ही डाक मतपत्रों को तैयार करना शुरू कर सकते हैं। दूसरों में, वे चुनाव के दिन तक शुरुआत नहीं कर सकते, जिससे काम पीछे चला जाता है।

segments.src: - **Deadlines for late-arriving ballots differ.** Some states accept mail ballots that arrive after Election Day as long as they were postmarked on time. Others require ballots to arrive by the close of polls. Where a grace period exists, the final count cannot be known until it ends.
segments.tr: - **देर से आने वाले मतपत्रों की समय-सीमा भिन्न होती है।** कुछ राज्य चुनाव के दिन के बाद आने वाले डाक मतपत्रों को तब तक स्वीकार करते हैं जब तक कि उन पर समय से डाक-मुहर (postmark) लगी हो। दूसरों के लिए आवश्यक है कि मतपत्र मतदान समाप्त होने तक पहुँच जाएं। जहाँ छूट की अवधि होती है, वहाँ इसके समाप्त होने तक अंतिम गिनती का पता नहीं चल सकता।

segments.src: - **Voters can fix some problems.** Many states let voters correct issues such as a missing signature through a process often called "curing." Provisional ballots, which are used when a voter's eligibility needs to be confirmed, are also reviewed after Election Day.
segments.tr: - **मतदाता कुछ समस्याओं को ठीक कर सकते हैं।** कई राज्य मतदाताओं को गायब हस्ताक्षर जैसी समस्याओं को एक प्रक्रिया के माध्यम से ठीक करने की अनुमति देते हैं जिसे अक्सर "क्यूरिंग" (सुधार) कहा जाता है। अनंतिम (प्रोविज़नल) मतपत्र, जिनका उपयोग तब किया जाता है जब मतदाता की पात्रता की पुष्टि करने की आवश्यकता होती है, उनकी भी चुनाव के दिन के बाद समीक्षा की जाती है।

segments.src: - **Counties report at different speeds.** A small county with few ballots may finish within hours. A large, populous county may take much longer. The order in which counties report can make a race appear to swing even though no individual vote has changed.
segments.tr: - **काउंटी अलग-अलग गति से रिपोर्ट करती हैं।** कम मतपत्रों वाली एक छोटी काउंटी घंटों के भीतर काम पूरा कर सकती है। एक बड़ी, घनी आबादी वाली काउंटी में बहुत अधिक समय लग सकता है। काउंटियों द्वारा रिपोर्ट करने का क्रम किसी मुकाबले को बदलता हुआ दिखा सकता है, भले ही किसी व्यक्तिगत वोट में बदलाव न हुआ हो।

segments.src: ## Why early tallies can shift
segments.tr: ## शुरुआती आंकड़ों में बदलाव क्यों आ सकता है

segments.src: Early totals can look lopsided for a simple reason: the votes counted first are not a random sample of all votes.
segments.tr: एक साधारण कारण से शुरुआती कुल आंकड़े एकतरफा दिख सकते हैं: सबसे पहले गिने गए वोट सभी वोटों का एक यादृच्छिक नमूना नहीं होते हैं।

segments.src: Which ballots come in first depends on the state's rules and on how each county reports.
segments.tr: कौन से मतपत्र पहले आते हैं यह राज्य के नियमों और प्रत्येक काउंटी की रिपोर्टिंग शैली पर निर्भर करता है।

segments.src: In one state, in-person votes may be tallied first, followed by mail ballots.
segments.tr: एक राज्य में, व्यक्तिगत रूप से डाले गए वोटों की गिनती पहले हो सकती है, उसके बाद डाक मतपत्रों की।

segments.src: In another, early and mail votes may be released first, and Election Day votes later.
segments.tr: दूसरे में, शुरुआती और डाक वोट पहले जारी किए जा सकते हैं, और चुनाव के दिन के वोट बाद में।

segments.src: Either way, the leader at 10 p.m.
segments.tr: जो भी हो, रात 10 बजे का लीडर

segments.src: may not be the leader once everything is counted.
segments.tr: सब कुछ गिने जाने के बाद लीडर नहीं भी रह सकता है।

segments.src: Analysts sometimes call this a "red shift" or "blue shift," depending on which direction it runs, but the direction varies by state and by year.
segments.tr: विश्लेषक कभी-कभी इसे "रेड शिफ्ट" या "ब्लू शिफ्ट" कहते हैं, जो इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि यह किस दिशा में जाता है, लेकिन यह दिशा राज्य और वर्ष के अनुसार भिन्न होती है।

segments.src: The shift reflects the order of reporting, not irregularities.
segments.tr: यह बदलाव रिपोर्टिंग के क्रम को दर्शाता है, गड़बड़ियों को नहीं।

segments.src: ## How the order of counting varies by state
segments.tr: ## गिनती का क्रम राज्य के अनुसार कैसे बदलता है

segments.src: States set their own election procedures, so there is no single national timeline.
segments.tr: राज्य अपनी स्वयं की चुनाव प्रक्रियाएँ निर्धारित करते हैं, इसलिए कोई एक राष्ट्रीय समय-सीमा नहीं है।

segments.src: These are general patterns, and details change, so always check your own state's election office.
segments.tr: ये सामान्य पैटर्न हैं, और विवरण बदलते रहते हैं, इसलिए हमेशा अपने राज्य के चुनाव कार्यालय से जाँच करें।

segments.src: - **States that process mail ballots early** often report a large share of results quickly, because most ballots are ready to be tabulated when polls close.
segments.tr: - **जो राज्य डाक मतपत्रों को जल्दी संसाधित करते हैं** वे अक्सर परिणामों का एक बड़ा हिस्सा जल्दी रिपोर्ट करते हैं, क्योंकि अधिकांश मतपत्र मतदान समाप्त होने पर सारणीबद्ध (tabulated) होने के लिए तैयार होते हैं।

segments.src: - **States that restrict early processing** tend to report in stages, with a large batch of mail ballots appearing later in the night or in the following days.
segments.tr: - **जो राज्य शुरुआती प्रसंस्करण को प्रतिबंधित करते हैं** वे चरणों में रिपोर्ट करते हैं, जिसमें डाक मतपत्रों का एक बड़ा समूह रात में बाद में या अगले दिनों में दिखाई देता है।

segments.src: - **States with grace periods for mail ballots** may not be able to finalize results until the deadline for late-arriving ballots passes.
segments.tr: - **डाक मतपत्रों के लिए छूट अवधि वाले राज्य** देर से आने वाले मतपत्रों की समय-सीमा बीत जाने तक परिणामों को अंतिम रूप देने में सक्षम नहीं हो सकते हैं।

segments.src: - **States with high volumes of mail voting** may need extra days simply because of the number of envelopes to process.
segments.tr: - **डाक मतदान की उच्च मात्रा वाले राज्यों** को केवल संसाधित करने वाले लिफाफों की संख्या के कारण अतिरिक्त दिनों की आवश्यकता हो सकती है।

segments.src: Rules change from one election cycle to the next, so last cycle's timeline is a useful guide but not a guarantee.
segments.tr: नियम एक चुनाव चक्र से दूसरे चुनाव चक्र में बदलते हैं, इसलिए पिछले चक्र की समय-सीमा एक उपयोगी मार्गदर्शिका है लेकिन कोई गारंटी नहीं है।

segments.src: ## How news organizations decide a race is over
segments.tr: ## समाचार संगठन कैसे तय करते हैं कि मुकाबला समाप्त हो गया है

segments.src: When a news organization says a candidate has won, it is making a projection, not announcing a certified result.
segments.tr: जब कोई समाचार संगठन कहता है कि किसी उम्मीदवार ने जीत हासिल की है, तो वह एक अनुमान लगा रहा होता है, प्रमाणित परिणाम की घोषणा नहीं कर रहा होता है।

segments.src: Newsrooms and the Associated Press use vote counts, the number of ballots still outstanding, where those ballots are from, and historical voting patterns to judge whether a trailing candidate can still catch up.
segments.tr: न्यूज़रूम और Associated Press वोटों की गिनती, अभी भी बकाया मतपत्रों की संख्या, वे मतपत्र कहाँ से हैं, और ऐतिहासिक मतदान पैटर्न का उपयोग यह आंकने के लिए करते हैं कि क्या पीछे चल रहा उम्मीदवार अभी भी बराबरी कर सकता है।

segments.src: A race is typically called only when the remaining ballots cannot plausibly change the outcome.
segments.tr: किसी मुकाबले का परिणाम आमतौर पर तभी घोषित किया जाता है जब शेष मतपत्र तार्किक रूप से परिणाम नहीं बदल सकते।

segments.src: Calls can differ by outlet.
segments.tr: विभिन्न आउटलेट के अनुमान अलग-अलग हो सकते हैं।

segments.src: A close race may stay uncalled for days, and that caution is deliberate.
segments.tr: एक कड़ा मुकाबला कई दिनों तक अनिर्णीत रह सकता है, और यह सावधानी जानबूझकर बरती जाती है।

segments.src: ## Close races, recounts and audits
segments.tr: ## कड़े मुकाबले, पुनर्गणना और ऑडिट

segments.src: When the margin is very narrow, a recount may happen automatically under state law or at the request of a candidate.
segments.tr: जब अंतर बहुत कम होता है, तो राज्य के कानून के तहत या किसी उम्मीदवार के अनुरोध पर स्वचालित रूप से पुनर्गणना (recount) हो सकती है।

segments.src: Many states also run post-election audits, which check a sample of ballots against the machine totals to confirm the equipment counted accurately.
segments.tr: कई राज्य चुनाव के बाद ऑडिट भी चलाते हैं, जो यह पुष्टि करने के लिए मशीन के योग के खिलाफ मतपत्रों के एक नमूने की जांच करते हैं कि उपकरण ने सटीक गिनती की है।

segments.src: Recounts rarely change the result by more than a small number of votes, but they can add time before a race is settled.
segments.tr: पुनर्गणना से परिणाम में शायद ही कभी कुछ वोटों से अधिक का बदलाव होता है, लेकिन वे मुकाबला तय होने से पहले समय बढ़ा सकते हैं।

segments.src: ## What to watch before declaring any race over
segments.tr: ## किसी भी मुकाबले को समाप्त घोषित करने से पहले क्या देखना चाहिए

segments.src: A few questions can help you read election night results sensibly:
segments.tr: कुछ प्रश्न आपको चुनाव की रात के परिणामों को समझदारी से पढ़ने में मदद कर सकते हैं:

segments.src: 1. **How much of the vote is in?** A percentage reporting figure helps, but it can mislead if the remaining ballots come from areas that lean differently.
segments.tr: 1. **कितने प्रतिशत वोटों की गिनती हो चुकी है?** रिपोर्टिंग का प्रतिशत आंकड़ा मदद करता है, लेकिन यह गुमराह कर सकता है यदि शेष मतपत्र ऐसे क्षेत्रों से आते हैं जिनका झुकाव अलग है।

segments.src: 2. **Which ballots are outstanding?** Mail ballots, provisional ballots and ballots from large counties can all change a total.
segments.tr: 2. **कौन से मतपत्र बकाया हैं?** डाक मतपत्र, अनंतिम (प्रोविज़नल) मतपत्र और बड़ी काउंटियों के मतपत्र सभी कुल योग को बदल सकते हैं।

segments.src: 3. **What are the state's deadlines?** Check whether late-arriving mail ballots will still be counted and when canvassing ends.
segments.tr: 3. **राज्य की अंतिम समय-सीमाएं क्या हैं?** जांचें कि क्या देर से आने वाले डाक मतपत्रों की गिनती अभी भी की जाएगी और कैनवासिंग कब समाप्त होगी।

segments.src: 4. **What is the margin?** A large lead with few ballots left is very different from a narrow lead with many left.
segments.tr: 4. **अंतर कितना है?** बहुत कम मतपत्रों के शेष रहने पर एक बड़ी बढ़त, बहुत सारे मतपत्रों के शेष रहने पर एक मामूली बढ़त से बहुत अलग होती है।

segments.src: 5. **Who is reporting the result?** Rely on your state or county election office for official information, and on established news organizations for projections.
segments.tr: 5. **परिणाम की रिपोर्ट कौन कर रहा है?** आधिकारिक जानकारी के लिए अपने राज्य या काउंटी चुनाव कार्यालय पर और अनुमानों के लिए स्थापित समाचार संगठनों पर भरोसा करें।

segments.src: ## Practical tips for voters
segments.tr: ## मतदाताओं के लिए व्यावहारिक सुझाव

segments.src: - Expect that some races will not be called on election night, and treat that as normal.
segments.tr: - उम्मीद रखें कि चुनाव की रात कुछ मुकाबलों के परिणाम घोषित नहीं होंगे, और इसे सामान्य मानें।

segments.src: - Look up your state's election office website for its timeline for counting, curing and certification.
segments.tr: - गिनती, सुधार (curing) और प्रमाणीकरण की समय-सीमा के लिए अपने राज्य के चुनाव कार्यालय की वेबसाइट देखें।

segments.src: - Be cautious about screenshots and unverified claims on social media, especially in the hours when totals are changing fast.
segments.tr: - सोशल मीडिया पर स्क्रीनशॉट और असत्यापित दावों के बारे में सतर्क रहें, खासकर उन घंटों में जब कुल आंकड़े तेज़ी से बदल रहे हों।

segments.src: - Remember that "not yet counted" is not the same as "missing" or "lost."
segments.tr: - याद रखें कि "अभी तक गिना नहीं गया" का अर्थ "गायब" या "खो गया" नहीं है।

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## मुख्य बात

segments.src: A slow count is not a failed count.
segments.tr: धीमी गिनती एक असफल गिनती नहीं है।

segments.src: Accuracy takes time, and the steps that take the longest, such as verifying mail ballots, curing errors and canvassing, are the same steps that protect the integrity of the result.
segments.tr: सटीकता में समय लगता है, और जिन चरणों में सबसे अधिक समय लगता है, जैसे कि डाक मतपत्रों का सत्यापन करना, त्रुटियों को सुधारना और कैनवासिंग करना, वे वही चरण हैं जो परिणाम की निष्ठा की रक्षा करते हैं।

segments.src: When you follow election night coverage, treat early totals as a snapshot, pay attention to what is still outstanding, and wait for officials to certify the final numbers.
segments.tr: जब आप चुनाव की रात की कवरेज का पालन करते हैं, तो शुरुआती आंकड़ों को एक स्नैपशॉट के रूप में समझें, इस बात पर ध्यान दें कि क्या अभी भी बकाया है, और अधिकारियों द्वारा अंतिम आंकड़ों को प्रमाणित करने की प्रतीक्षा करें।

segments.src: *This article is for general information only and does not describe the rules of any specific jurisdiction.
segments.tr: *यह लेख केवल सामान्य जानकारी के लिए है और किसी विशिष्ट अधिकार क्षेत्र के नियमों का वर्णन नहीं करता है।

segments.src: Check your local election office for current procedures and deadlines.*
segments.tr: वर्तमान प्रक्रियाओं और समय-सीमाओं के लिए अपने स्थानीय चुनाव कार्यालय की जाँच करें।*

es.title: Por qué la noche de las elecciones rara vez termina en la noche de las elecciones: cómo se cuentan los votos y cuándo esperar los resultados

segments.src: For many Americans, election night means staying up late, watching a map fill in with color and waiting for a winner to be named.
segments.tr: Para muchos estadounidenses, la noche de las elecciones significa quedarse despierto hasta tarde, ver cómo un mapa se llena de color y esperar a que se nombre a un ganador.

segments.src: In practice, the picture on election night is often incomplete.
segments.tr: En la práctica, el panorama en la noche de las elecciones suele estar incompleto.

segments.src: Counting continues for days in some places, and that is usually a sign the system is working as designed, not a sign that something has gone wrong.
segments.tr: El conteo continúa durante días en algunos lugares, y eso suele ser una señal de que el sistema está funcionando como fue diseñado, no una señal de que algo haya salido mal.

segments.src: This guide explains why results take time, how counting differs from state to state, and what to look for before treating any early tally as final.
segments.tr: Esta guía explica por qué los resultados toman tiempo, cómo difiere el conteo de un estado a otro y qué buscar antes de tratar cualquier recuento inicial como definitivo.

segments.src: ## Unofficial results come first, official results come later
segments.tr: ## Los resultados no oficiales llegan primero, los resultados oficiales llegan después

segments.src: The numbers you see on election night are **unofficial**.
segments.tr: Los números que ve en la noche de las elecciones son **no oficiales**.

segments.src: News organizations and election offices report running totals as counties finish processing ballots.
segments.tr: Las organizaciones de noticias y las oficinas electorales informan los totales parciales a medida que los condados terminan de procesar las boletas.

segments.src: Official results come only after a process called **canvassing**, in which local and state officials check the totals, reconcile them against records of voters and ballots, and certify the outcome.
segments.tr: Los resultados oficiales llegan solo después de un proceso llamado **escrutinio** (canvassing), en el cual los funcionarios locales y estatales verifican los totales, los concilian con los registros de votantes y boletas, y certifican el resultado.

segments.src: Canvassing and certification can take from several days to several weeks, depending on the state.
segments.tr: El escrutinio y la certificación pueden tomar desde varios días hasta varias semanas, dependiendo del estado.

segments.src: During that period, officials add late-arriving ballots, resolve problems with incomplete ballots, and correct clerical errors.
segments.tr: Durante ese período, los funcionarios agregan las boletas que llegan tarde, resuelven problemas con boletas incompletas y corrigen errores administrativos.

segments.src: Small changes in totals during this stage are normal.
segments.tr: Los pequeños cambios en los totales durante esta etapa son normales.

segments.src: ## Why counting takes time
segments.tr: ## Por qué el conteo toma tiempo

segments.src: Several things make a fast count hard.
segments.tr: Varias cosas hacen que un conteo rápido sea difícil.

segments.src: - **Mail ballots take more steps to process.** A ballot returned by mail usually needs its envelope opened, its signature or identifying information checked, the ballot removed, flattened and scanned, and the voter's record updated. An in-person ballot cast on a machine skips most of these steps.
segments.tr: - **Las boletas por correo requieren más pasos para ser procesadas.** Una boleta devuelta por correo generalmente necesita que se abra su sobre, se verifique su firma o información de identificación, se extraiga la boleta, se aplane y se escanee, y se actualice el registro del votante. Una boleta emitida en persona en una máquina omite la mayoría de estos pasos.

segments.src: - **Rules about when processing can begin differ.** In some states, election workers may start preparing mail ballots weeks before Election Day. In others, they may not begin until Election Day itself, which pushes the work back.
segments.tr: - **Las reglas sobre cuándo puede comenzar el procesamiento difieren.** En algunos estados, los trabajadores electorales pueden comenzar a preparar las boletas por correo semanas antes del día de las elecciones. En otros, es posible que no comiencen hasta el mismo día de las elecciones, lo que retrasa el trabajo.

segments.src: - **Deadlines for late-arriving ballots differ.** Some states accept mail ballots that arrive after Election Day as long as they were postmarked on time. Others require ballots to arrive by the close of polls. Where a grace period exists, the final count cannot be known until it ends.
segments.tr: - **Los plazos para las boletas que llegan tarde difieren.** Algunos estados aceptan boletas por correo que llegan después del día de las elecciones siempre que tengan el matasellos a tiempo. Otros requieren que las boletas lleguen antes del cierre de las urnas. Donde existe un período de gracia, el conteo final no puede conocerse hasta que este termine.

segments.src: - **Voters can fix some problems.** Many states let voters correct issues such as a missing signature through a process often called "curing." Provisional ballots, which are used when a voter's eligibility needs to be confirmed, are also reviewed after Election Day.
segments.tr: - **Los votantes pueden solucionar algunos problemas.** Muchos estados permiten que los votantes corrijan problemas como una firma faltante a través de un proceso a menudo llamado "subsanación" (curing). Las boletas provisionales, que se utilizan cuando se necesita confirmar la elegibilidad de un votante, también se revisan después del día de las elecciones.

segments.src: - **Counties report at different speeds.** A small county with few ballots may finish within hours. A large, populous county may take much longer. The order in which counties report can make a race appear to swing even though no individual vote has changed.
segments.tr: - **Los condados informan a diferentes velocidades.** Un condado pequeño con pocas boletas puede terminar en cuestión de horas. Un condado grande y poblado puede tardar mucho más. El orden en que los condados informan puede hacer que una contienda parezca cambiar incluso si ningún voto individual ha cambiado.

segments.src: ## Why early tallies can shift
segments.tr: ## Por qué los recuentos iniciales pueden cambiar

segments.src: Early totals can look lopsided for a simple reason: the votes counted first are not a random sample of all votes.
segments.tr: Los totales iniciales pueden parecer desiguales por una razón simple: los votos contados primero no son una muestra aleatoria de todos los votos.

segments.src: Which ballots come in first depends on the state's rules and on how each county reports.
segments.tr: Qué boletas llegan primero depende de las reglas del estado y de cómo informa cada condado.

segments.src: In one state, in-person votes may be tallied first, followed by mail ballots.
segments.tr: En un estado, los votos en persona pueden ser contados primero, seguidos por las boletas por correo.

segments.src: In another, early and mail votes may be released first, and Election Day votes later.
segments.tr: En otro, los votos anticipados y por correo pueden publicarse primero, y los votos del día de las elecciones más tarde.

segments.src: Either way, the leader at 10 p.m.
segments.tr: De cualquier manera, el líder a las 10 p.m.

segments.src: may not be the leader once everything is counted.
segments.tr: puede no ser el líder una vez que todo esté contado.

segments.src: Analysts sometimes call this a "red shift" or "blue shift," depending on which direction it runs, but the direction varies by state and by year.
segments.tr: Los analistas a veces llaman a esto un "desplazamiento rojo" (red shift) o "desplazamiento azul" (blue shift), dependiendo de la dirección en la que ocurra, pero la dirección varía según el estado y el año.

segments.src: The shift reflects the order of reporting, not irregularities.
segments.tr: El cambio refleja el orden de los informes, no irregularidades.

segments.src: ## How the order of counting varies by state
segments.tr: ## Cómo varía el orden del conteo según el estado

segments.src: States set their own election procedures, so there is no single national timeline.
segments.tr: Los estados establecen sus propios procedimientos electorales, por lo que no existe un cronograma nacional único.

segments.src: These are general patterns, and details change, so always check your own state's election office.
segments.tr: Estos son patrones generales, y los detalles cambian, así que siempre consulte la oficina electoral de su propio estado.

segments.src: - **States that process mail ballots early** often report a large share of results quickly, because most ballots are ready to be tabulated when polls close.
segments.tr: - **Los estados que procesan las boletas por correo temprano** a menudo informan una gran parte de los resultados rápidamente, porque la mayoría de las boletas están listas para ser tabuladas cuando cierran las urnas.

segments.src: - **States that restrict early processing** tend to report in stages, with a large batch of mail ballots appearing later in the night or in the following days.
segments.tr: - **Los estados que restringen el procesamiento temprano** tienden a informar en etapas, con un gran lote de boletas por correo apareciendo más tarde en la noche o en los días siguientes.

segments.src: - **States with grace periods for mail ballots** may not be able to finalize results until the deadline for late-arriving ballots passes.
segments.tr: - **Los estados con períodos de gracia para las boletas por correo** pueden no poder finalizar los resultados hasta que pase la fecha límite para las boletas que llegan tarde.

segments.src: - **States with high volumes of mail voting** may need extra days simply because of the number of envelopes to process.
segments.tr: - **Los estados con grandes volúmenes de votación por correo** pueden necesitar días adicionales simplemente debido a la cantidad de sobres que deben procesar.

segments.src: Rules change from one election cycle to the next, so last cycle's timeline is a useful guide but not a guarantee.
segments.tr: Las reglas cambian de un ciclo electoral a otro, por lo que el cronograma del ciclo anterior es una guía útil pero no una garantía.

segments.src: ## How news organizations decide a race is over
segments.tr: ## Cómo deciden las organizaciones de noticias que una contienda ha terminado

segments.src: When a news organization says a candidate has won, it is making a projection, not announcing a certified result.
segments.tr: Cuando una organización de noticias dice que un candidato ha ganado, está haciendo una proyección, no anunciando un resultado certificado.

segments.src: Newsrooms and the Associated Press use vote counts, the number of ballots still outstanding, where those ballots are from, and historical voting patterns to judge whether a trailing candidate can still catch up.
segments.tr: Las salas de redacción y Associated Press utilizan los conteos de votos, la cantidad de boletas aún pendientes, de dónde provienen esas boletas y los patrones históricos de votación para juzgar si un candidato que va perdiendo aún puede alcanzar al líder.

segments.src: A race is typically called only when the remaining ballots cannot plausibly change the outcome.
segments.tr: Una contienda generalmente se declara solo cuando las boletas restantes no pueden cambiar plausiblemente el resultado.

segments.src: Calls can differ by outlet.
segments.tr: Las declaraciones pueden diferir según el medio.

segments.src: A close race may stay uncalled for days, and that caution is deliberate.
segments.tr: Una contienda reñida puede permanecer sin declararse durante días, y esa precaución es deliberada.

segments.src: ## Close races, recounts and audits
segments.tr: ## Contiendas reñidas, recuentos y auditorías

segments.src: When the margin is very narrow, a recount may happen automatically under state law or at the request of a candidate.
segments.tr: Cuando el margen es muy estrecho, puede ocurrir un recuento automáticamente bajo la ley estatal o a solicitud de un candidato.

segments.src: Many states also run post-election audits, which check a sample of ballots against the machine totals to confirm the equipment counted accurately.
segments.tr: Muchos estados también realizan auditorías postelectorales, que verifican una muestra de boletas contra los totales de las máquinas para confirmar que el equipo contó con precisión.

segments.src: Recounts rarely change the result by more than a small number of votes, but they can add time before a race is settled.
segments.tr: Los recuentos rara vez cambian el resultado por más de un pequeño número de votos, pero pueden añadir tiempo antes de que se resuelva una contienda.

segments.src: ## What to watch before declaring any race over
segments.tr: ## Qué observar antes de declarar que cualquier contienda ha terminado

segments.src: A few questions can help you read election night results sensibly:
segments.tr: Algunas preguntas pueden ayudarle a leer los resultados de la noche de las elecciones de manera sensata:

segments.src: 1. **How much of the vote is in?** A percentage reporting figure helps, but it can mislead if the remaining ballots come from areas that lean differently.
segments.tr: 1. **¿Qué porcentaje del voto se ha contabilizado?** Una cifra de porcentaje de informes ayuda, pero puede inducir a error si las boletas restantes provienen de áreas que tienen una inclinación diferente.

segments.src: 2. **Which ballots are outstanding?** Mail ballots, provisional ballots and ballots from large counties can all change a total.
segments.tr: 2. **¿Qué boletas están pendientes?** Las boletas por correo, las boletas provisionales y las boletas de condados grandes pueden cambiar un total.

segments.src: 3. **What are the state's deadlines?** Check whether late-arriving mail ballots will still be counted and when canvassing ends.
segments.tr: 3. **¿Cuáles son los plazos del estado?** Verifique si las boletas por correo que llegan tarde aún se contarán y cuándo termina el escrutinio.

segments.src: 4. **What is the margin?** A large lead with few ballots left is very different from a narrow lead with many left.
segments.tr: 4. **¿Cuál es el margen?** Una ventaja grande con pocas boletas restantes es muy diferente de una ventaja estrecha con muchas boletas restantes.

segments.src: 5. **Who is reporting the result?** Rely on your state or county election office for official information, and on established news organizations for projections.
segments.tr: 5. **¿Quién informa el resultado?** Confíe en su oficina electoral estatal o del condado para obtener información oficial, y en organizaciones de noticias establecidas para las proyecciones.

segments.src: ## Practical tips for voters
segments.tr: ## Consejos prácticos para los votantes

segments.src: - Expect that some races will not be called on election night, and treat that as normal.
segments.tr: - Espere que algunas contiendas no se declaren en la noche de las elecciones, y trate eso como algo normal.

segments.src: - Look up your state's election office website for its timeline for counting, curing and certification.
segments.tr: - Busque el sitio web de la oficina electoral de su estado para conocer su cronograma de conteo, subsanación y certificación.

segments.src: - Be cautious about screenshots and unverified claims on social media, especially in the hours when totals are changing fast.
segments.tr: - Sea cauteloso con las capturas de pantalla y las afirmaciones no verificadas en las redes sociales, especialmente en las horas en que los totales cambian rápidamente.

segments.src: - Remember that "not yet counted" is not the same as "missing" or "lost."
segments.tr: - Recuerde que "aún no contado" no es lo mismo que "faltante" o "perdido".

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## En resumen

segments.src: A slow count is not a failed count.
segments.tr: Un conteo lento no es un conteo fallido.

segments.src: Accuracy takes time, and the steps that take the longest, such as verifying mail ballots, curing errors and canvassing, are the same steps that protect the integrity of the result.
segments.tr: La precisión toma tiempo, y los pasos que toman más tiempo, como verificar las boletas por correo, subsanar errores y realizar el escrutinio, son los mismos pasos que protegen la integridad del resultado.

segments.src: When you follow election night coverage, treat early totals as a snapshot, pay attention to what is still outstanding, and wait for officials to certify the final numbers.
segments.tr: Cuando siga la cobertura de la noche de las elecciones, trate los totales iniciales como una instantánea, preste atención a lo que aún está pendiente y espere a que los funcionarios certifiquen los números finales.

segments.src: Check your local election office for current procedures and deadlines.*
segments.tr: Consulte a su oficina electoral local para conocer los procedimientos y plazos actuales.*

segments.tr: بالنسبة للعديد من الأمريكيين، تعني ليلة الانتخابات السهر لتقنية متأخرة، ومتابعة الخريطة وهي تكتسي بالألوان والانتظار حتى يتم إعلان الفائز.

segments.src: In practice, the picture on election night is often incomplete.

segments.src: Counting continues for days in some places, and that is usually a sign the system is working as designed, not a sign that something has gone wrong.
segments.tr: يستمر فرز الأصوات لأيام في بعض الأماكن، وعادة ما يكون ذلك علامة على أن النظام يعمل كما هو مخطط له، وليس علامة على حدوث خلل ما.

segments.src: ## Unofficial results come first, official results come later
segments.tr: ## النتائج غير الرسمية تأتي أولاً، والنتائج الرسمية تأتي لاحقًا

segments.src: The numbers you see on election night are **unofficial**.
segments.tr: الأرقام التي تراها في ليلة الانتخابات هي أرقام **غير رسمية**.

segments.src: News organizations and election offices report running totals as counties finish processing ballots.
segments.tr: تنشر المؤسسات الإخبارية ومكاتب الانتخابات الإجماليات الجارية مع إكمال المقاطعات لمعالجة بطاقات الاقتراع.

segments.src: Official results come only after a process called **canvassing**, in which local and state officials check the totals, reconcile them against records of voters and ballots, and certify the outcome.
segments.tr: تأتي النتائج الرسمية فقط بعد عملية تُسمى **تدقيق النتائج (Canvassing)**، حيث يقوم المسؤولون المحليون والولائيون بمراجعة الإجماليات، ومطابقتها مع سجلات الناخبين وبطاقات الاقتراع، والتدقيق في النتيجة والمصادقة عليها.

segments.src: Canvassing and certification can take from several days to several weeks, depending on the state.
segments.tr: يمكن أن تستغرق عملية التدقيق والمصادقة من عدة أيام إلى عدة أسابيع، اعتمادًا على الولاية.

segments.src: During that period, officials add late-arriving ballots, resolve problems with incomplete ballots, and correct clerical errors.
segments.tr: خلال تلك الفترة، يضيف المسؤولون بطاقات الاقتراع الواصلة متأخرًا، ويحلون المشكلات المتعلقة ببطاقات الاقتراع غير المكتملة، ويصححون الأخطاء الكتابية.

segments.src: Small changes in totals during this stage are normal.
segments.tr: التغييرات الصغيرة في الإجماليات خلال هذه المرحلة هي أمر طبيعي.

segments.src: ## Why counting takes time
segments.tr: ## لماذا يستغرق الفرز وقتًا

segments.src: Several things make a fast count hard.
segments.tr: هناك عدة عوامل تجعل الفرز السريع أمرًا صعبًا.

segments.tr: - **تختلف القواعد حول وقت بدء المعالجة.** في بعض الولايات، قد يبدأ موظفو الانتخابات في تجهيز بطاقات الاقتراع عبر البريد قبل أسابيع من يوم الانتخابات. وفي ولايات أخرى، قد لا يبدأون حتى يوم الانتخابات نفسه، مما يؤدي إلى تأخير العمل.

segments.tr: ## لماذا يمكن أن تتغير الإحصاءات المبكرة

segments.tr: وفي ولاية أخرى، قد يتم نشر أصوات الاقتراع المبكر والبريد أولاً، وأصوات يوم الانتخابات لاحقًا.

segments.src: The shift reflects the order of reporting, not irregularities.

segments.src: ## How the order of counting varies by state
segments.tr: ## كيف يختلف ترتيب الفرز حسب الولاية

segments.src: States set their own election procedures, so there is no single national timeline.
segments.tr: تحدد الولايات إجراءاتها الانتخابية الخاصة، لذا لا يوجد جدول زمني وطني موحد.
